newsitem.title: UK: Brazilian airliner insured for $30 mln - industry.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian airliner insured for $30 mln - industry.

text.p: A Brazilian airliner which crashed on Thursday was insured for $30 million, London based insurance industry sources told Reuters.
The Fokker-100 aircraft slammed into houses in a densely populated area of Sao Paulo shortly after take-off, killing all 95 people on board and at least eight more on the ground.
The aircraft was built in 1993 and the risk was placed by broker Sedgwick Group Plc, the sources said, adding that there was liability insurance, but that they were unable to comment on the details.
The $30 million hull insurance was led by Lloyds of London aviation syndicate 925, which is managed by Ockham Holdings Plc, sources close to the company said.
Syndicate 925 underwriter Len Hudson was not available to comment, while a spokeswoman for Sedgwick said the company did not comment on individual incidents.
The industry sources said they would be surprised if the hull insurance was not widely placed in London, as is normally the case with aviation insurance.
Among the Brazilians who died on the plane were Alberto Coimbra Vieira, 51, corporate director of Banco Itau and Luiz Lauro Romero, head of the research at the National Development Bank (BNDES).
At least eight executives at private bank Unibanco were also on the plane, a company spokeswoman said.

Officials at Brazil's Civil Aviation Department (DAC), which is responsible for investigating the accident, said they had recovered the Fokker's two black boxes, which contain recordings of the pilot's last conversation with his crew and with air controllers. They said a final report on the accident would be published within 90 days.
